x: Fred Howe of Blackpool continued for a further 5 miles to set a World's best mark for 30 miles of 2:48:00.8, a first class effort. Whilst Barry was running, his 100 laps were being faithfully recorded by Jack Baker---having a rest before competing in the 10miles road race later in the day.
Last month he finished second to Fred Howe (ex-Blackpool) in the Victoria State marathon with 2:25:16 and is now managing to step up his mileage again.

The times tell the story though, 2.28.13 (9th), 2.31.32 (1st) and 2.37.27 (8th). Nevertheless these were times still good enough to put him ahead of Ron Clarke, Dave Power, Ian Sinfield and Fred Howe.
